description: Single-panel engineering tensile stress-strain plot labelled (d). The x-axis is "ε_E, Engineering strain, %" running 0-100 with ticks at 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100; the y-axis is "σ_E, Engineering stress, MPa" running 0-1500 with ticks at 0, 300, 600, 900, 1200, 1500. The legend header reads "Fe30MnxAl1C(1100°C)" and lists five coloured curves: 6Al (black), 8Al (red), 10Al (green), 11Al (navy), 12Al (cyan). The cyan 12Al curve rises almost vertically to a near-flat plateau between the 900 and 1200 MPa gridlines (~900-950 MPa), holds it, then drops abruptly near ~50% strain. The navy 11Al curve starts around the 600 MPa gridline and rises gradually toward ~850 MPa. The 6Al, 8Al and 10Al curves start progressively lower (black 6Al lowest, near 400 MPa), rise with a concave-down shape to a common peak region between 800 and 900 MPa, then fall; fracture strain increases as Al decreases, with 6Al failing near ~75%, 8Al near ~80% and 10Al near ~85-90%. The figure demonstrates that higher Al content raises the flow/plateau stress but reduces tensile elongation. No numeric data labels are printed on the curves.

observations.observation: The plot is a single engineering stress-strain curve set labelled panel (d), with y-axis 'σ_E, Engineering stress, MPa' (0-1500) and x-axis 'ε_E, Engineering strain, %' (0-100).
The legend header reads 'Fe30MnxAl1C(1100°C)', identifying the alloy family as Fe-30Mn-1C with variable Al, solution-treated at 1100°C.
The 12Al (cyan) curve reaches a near-flat plateau between the 900 and 1200 MPa gridlines and fractures abruptly near ~50% strain.
The 11Al (navy) curve yields around the 600 MPa gridline and rises gradually toward ~850 MPa.
The 6Al (black) curve starts lowest (near the 400 MPa region) and reaches its peak between 800 and 900 MPa before failing near ~75% strain.
The 8Al (red) and 10Al (green) curves also peak in the 800-900 MPa band, with 10Al (green) extending to the largest strain among the lower-Al curves, near ~85-90%.
Fracture/elongation increases as Al content decreases, whereas plateau (flow) stress increases as Al content increases.
No numeric value labels are printed on any curve; stress and strain values can only be read against the gridlines.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress-strain curves (σ_E vs ε_E) for Fe30MnxAl1C (1100°C) alloys with 6Al, 8Al, 10Al, 11Al and 12Al; x-axis 0-100% strain, y-axis 0-1500 MPa. Increasing Al raises the plateau stress (12Al ~900-950 MPa) but lowers elongation (12Al fractures ~50%, 6Al ~75%).
